notes.note: Reviewed changed ACP adapter source against the declared/observed/working and policy contracts. The added SDK-auth-required classifier only maps explicit engine refusal to a typed authentication error and settled startup refusal. It does not answer inbound credential callbacks, widen extension authority, add tool-policy enforcement, alter steering or reinstate the historical global ACP chat proposal. Historical observations remain dated; no vendor interoperability was rerun.

Reviewed ACPProcess launch-failure handling and ACPProbe first-contact behavior against onboarding direction. Missing executable fails as launch failure, deadline remains a bounded first-contact wait with background continuation; this does not make detection or handshake prove sign-in. Existing app-home credential import and profile custody, provider configuration and onboarding direction remain unchanged.

Reviewed merged ACP adapter/probe/process and registry setup against this guide: an exact SDK auth_required refusal becomes engine-sign-in-required at session start or turn; version/handshake never prove login. Missing launch and first-contact deadline messages name the engine, optional unknown login stays nonblocking, and background first contact preserves saved unregistered repair state. Registry GET retains login-shell detection and adds public listing facts; confirmed registry command passes through the setup flow and mutation result. No real sign-in, provider turn or production qualification claimed.

Reviewed changed ACP adapter against the claims in this document. Explicit SDK auth_required errors now report engine-sign-in-required with auth kind at startup/turn; unknown sign-in remains optional, and version/handshake are not authentication evidence. Session routing, model/tool delivery, delegation grants, configuration fields, CLI transport and station-control ownership remain unchanged. Public registry setup preserves command confirmation and first-contact result projection. This is bounded source review, not renewed live-provider or unrelated API qualification.
